title: NASA has moved its rockets to the pad on the same two crawlers since 1965

cover.alt: Side view of a huge grey tracked vehicle with a flat steel deck, rolling across a gravel road under a cloudy sky.

body: Kennedy Space Center's two **crawler-transporters** were built by the Marion Power Shovel Company for $14 million each, and on completion were the largest self-powered land vehicles in the world. Each weighs about 2,721 tonnes and rides on eight tracks, two at each corner, with 57 shoes per track and each shoe weighing about a tonne. Loaded, a crawler tops out at 1 mph (1.6 km/h). The same pair carried Saturn V rockets for Apollo, Space Shuttles from 1981 to 2011, and now NASA's Space Launch System.

slides.alt: A giant grey tracked vehicle with a flat steel deck rolls slowly across gravel, raising a haze of dust, then a low view across the gravel as it passes.
slides.caption: Kennedy Space Center, 2022: crawler-transporter 2, carrying nothing, rolls towards the Vehicle Assembly Building to fetch the Artemis I rocket.

slides.question: Loaded, it tops out at 1 mph. How many hours does a crawler take to carry a rocket to the pad?
slides.explanation: The average trip is about five hours, along crawlerways roughly 5.5 and 6.8 km long to pads 39A and 39B.

slides.label: of diesel burned per kilometre (125.7 US gallons a mile)
slides.text: Two V16 diesel engines drive generators that power 16 electric traction motors. The fuel tanks hold about 19,000 litres.

slides.heading: Keeping a rocket upright
slides.text: The ramp up to the launch pad climbs at a 5% slope. As the crawler climbs it, a laser guidance and levelling system raises or lowers each side so the launch platform stays level to within 0.16 degrees, which is no more than about 30 cm out at the top of a Saturn V.

slides.heading: Crawler-transporter 2's lifting capacity
slides.note: Upgraded to carry the heavier Space Launch System and its launch tower

slides.question: Why is the crawlerway paved with river rock?
options: It was the cheapest stone nearby
slides.explanation: The road is about 2 m deep and topped with Alabama and Tennessee river rock, chosen for its low friction to reduce the chance of sparks.
